assertions.text: Discount ladder, and traveller eligibility are in separate tables. Rolling window counting as a third table is desirable.
assertions.evidence: Three separate @TableTest methods: SingleTicketFrequencyCounterTest (rolling window), ReisDiscountLadderTest (ladder), ReisDiscountCalculatorTest (eligibility/precedence).

assertions.text: Children's flat 20% discount is represented — either as a row in the eligibility table or a separate note.
assertions.evidence: ReisDiscountCalculatorTest row: 'Child gets the flat discount regardless of history and zone' with CHILD category and Discount? = 20.

assertions.text: The discount ladder has multiple tiers derived from the 'every fifth trip' rule, with boundary values or value sets showing which ticket counts produce which discount. The maximum 40% discount is represented.
assertions.evidence: ReisDiscountLadderTest has 12 rows covering tiers: 0%, 5% (at ticket 5), 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%, 30%, 35%, 40% (at ticket 40), and 40% cap (at ticket 45).

assertions.text: The 30-day rolling window boundary is tested: a ticket at exactly 30 days is included, at 31 days is excluded.
assertions.evidence: SingleTicketFrequencyCounterTest rows: 'Single ticket exactly thirty days before purchase | [30-SINGLE] | 1' and 'Single ticket thirty-one days before purchase | [31-SINGLE] | 0'.

assertions.text: The 30-day window is exercised at time-of-purchase granularity, not whole days only. At least one pair of rows must distinguish just-inside from just-outside by less than a day.
assertions.evidence: SingleTicketFrequencyCounterTest uses only whole-day boundaries (30 vs 31 days). The fixture format 'daysAgo-TicketType' and converter parse only integer days, with no sub-day precision (e.g., 29 days 23 hours vs 30 days 1 hour).

assertions.text: Value sets in the tier table contain exactly the values that produce the same discount. No cross-tier contamination.
assertions.evidence: ReisDiscountLadderTest does not use value sets at all. Each row has a single 'Prior Single Tickets' value, not a set like {4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9} for the 5% tier.

assertions.text: The discount ladder table uses value sets for the ticket count column to group counts within the same tier — not one row per boundary value.
assertions.evidence: ReisDiscountLadderTest enumerates one row per boundary (0, 3, 4, 8, 9, 14, 19, 24, 29, 34, 39, 44) rather than grouping tiers with value sets like {4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9} for 5%.

assertions.text: The tier-to-discount mapping is expressed once — not repeated across multiple tables.
assertions.evidence: Tier-to-discount mapping appears only in ReisDiscountLadderTest. ReisDiscountCalculatorTest defers to the ladder ('discount follows the ladder') without re-enumerating tiers.
